decisions.approvalNote: The user explicitly approved Option A: Foundation v3 with a root-instance reusable theme profile and bounded per-asset overrides.
decisions.context: Foundation v2 cannot be amended without violating the accepted immutable-release architecture, and strict asset schemas reject undeclared configuration. All options therefore publish a v3 successor for completed property schemas and provide an explicit upgrade path for existing v2 systems. The choice determines how global style values are persisted, validated, inherited by previews, and overridden by individual assets. In every option, users edit semantic tokens through color pickers and allowlisted dropdowns; they do not edit arbitrary CSS text.

consequences: Publish Foundation v3 definitions and backing resources with completed renderer property schemas.
Add allowlisted semantic color, typography, spacing, button, form, and surface tokens to the system root.
Map inherited tokens and per-asset overrides to generated CSS custom properties and stable style-role classes in the shared preview.
options.label: Foundation v3 with a root-instance theme profile
options.summary: Declare the reusable theme profile on the v3 system-root asset configuration, inherit it through the composed preview tree, and declare bounded per-asset override fields only where relevant.
tradeoffs: Reuses the existing selected-configuration, validation, undo, revision-save, reload, and build paths.
Keeps one system-scoped style source without introducing another composition node.
Requires a dedicated Styling editor for a structured root configuration field and an explicit v2-to-v3 upgrade action.

consequences: Publish Foundation v3 property schemas plus a new theme asset definition and binding contract.
Add validation that a visual system has exactly one effective theme binding.
Keep per-asset overrides in each visual asset's declared configuration.
options.label: Foundation v3 with a dedicated theme asset
options.summary: Represent the reusable style profile as a nonvisual Foundation asset that is bound to the system root and consumed by visual descendants.
tradeoffs: Makes themes independently reusable and conceptually asset-native.
Adds theme discovery, binding, uniqueness, inheritance, upgrade, and placement semantics to an already complex composition graph.
Requires the inspector to coordinate selection of a visual asset with editing a different bound theme asset.

consequences: Migrate every revision transport and persistence path for the new profile.
Maintain a second schema and validator for styling outside asset configuration.
Bridge revision-level tokens into the shared asset preview and build output.
options.label: Foundation v3 plus a revision-level style profile
options.summary: Add a style-profile field directly to the System Builder revision contract while using v3 only for the completed per-asset property schemas.
tradeoffs: Separates system-wide presentation from the root asset and makes theme availability unconditional.
Expands contracts, persistence adapters, use cases, IPC/HTTP clients, import/export, and qualification surfaces.
Duplicates configuration validation concepts outside the Asset Kernel and weakens asset portability.

plan.summary: Build Foundation v3 additively in three cohesive chunks: isolate immutable version boundaries and create v3 catalogs, complete presentation/theme schemas through a single audited projection, then wire all current consumers and qualify exact-version coexistence and backing resources.

risks: An incomplete replacement of v2 hard-coded current-manifest imports could make v3 assets unavailable in Composer or structure validation.
Changing v2 version sources before isolating them could alter published v2 definition fingerprints and backing resources.

A root theme object would fall back to a JSON editor unless the Styling panel owns its bounded controls; v3 fields must therefore carry explicit presentation metadata and remain unavailable as raw CSS.
Adding fields without matching defaults and preview/backing-resource descriptors could reintroduce schema-renderer drift.
Default no-version lookups currently prefer legacy descriptors in some catalogs and must become intentionally current-first without breaking exact-version reads.
research.summary: Foundation v2 is produced by recursively replacing v1 version strings and adding v2 layout/slot definitions. Several layout files and current services import SYSTEM_FOUNDATION_CURRENT_PACK_VERSION or SYSTEM_FOUNDATION_PACK_V2_MANIFEST directly, so changing the current constant without first introducing a dedicated v2 constant would mutate the supposedly immutable v2 release. The functional-default and backing-resource catalogs are also explicitly two-version maps. A complete v3 implementation therefore needs an additive exact-version catalog, version-aware functional/backing resources, and current-manifest consumers that do not name v2. The frontend audit covers 77 assets; the only empty strict schemas are the 13 conversation definitions, while other families already carry rich schemas. The preview surface still contains fixed conversation content and consumes a bounded set of configuration keys, so v3 can complete those schemas and add semantic style fields without raw CSS.
